title: Memory file frontmatter contract (System A — curated file-memory)
description: YAML frontmatter contract every file under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/*.md MUST carry. Codifies the System-A curated-memory frontmatter contract. Schema validates the frontmatter block parsed as an object; additionalProperties is true so memory files may carry per-type extensions alongside the universal fields.

_design_notes.purpose: Codify the two-axis memory contract: filename prefix carries provenance, the `type:` frontmatter field carries retrieval axis. Foundation-repo only; adopter live memory cutover is OUT OF SCOPE.

provenance_axis_filename_prefix.description: Filename prefix declares where a memory originated (preserved muscle memory + grep patterns + retroactive compatibility). Convention: <prefix>_<kebab-slug>.md.

mapping.user_*: Identity, preferences, conventions. Default type: semantic.
mapping.feedback_*: Lessons-from-incident OR workflow rules. Default type: procedural (LangMem defines procedural memory as the agent updating its own instructions from accumulated feedback; reflection rides this provenance prefix, not a separate retrieval type).
mapping.project_*: Active-project context, decisions, status. Default type: semantic; may mix in episodic for session-specific records.
mapping.reference_*: External-system pointers (Linear project, Grafana dashboard, repo URL, etc.). Default type: semantic.
mapping.episode_*: Session-outcome capture (CoALA situation/thought/action/result). Always type: episodic. Authored by hooks/session-episode-write.sh.

retrieval_axis_type_field.description: The `type:` frontmatter field declares retrieval-axis classification. Drives MEMORY.md template grouping, single 180d re-validation staleness signal, and future retrieval-shaped operations.

values.semantic: Facts, preferences, conventions, identity. Stable knowledge.
values.episodic: Session/event records, decision narratives. Time-anchored. Never decays.
values.procedural: Workflow rules with explicit steps + their rationale. Imperative knowledge; absorbs lessons-from-incident (the feedback_ corpus).

revalidation_interval_days._description: Single re-validation interval. Per-type half-lives are deferred to v1.1 — a single 180-day interval applies to all non-episodic memory. Consumed by the librarian memory-staleness capability; flags entries where last_validated exceeds the interval (propose-only, never deletes). Per-file `confidence` and explicit operator override at run time both supersede the default.

body_conventions._description: Markdown body shape is NOT validated by this JSON Schema (no JSON path into body bytes). Conventions are documentary; regression tests verify body-shape compliance for episodic entries only.
body_conventions.feedback_procedural: Rule sentence (lead) + **Why:** (incident/preference rationale; 1-2 lines) + **How to apply:** (edge-case judgment; 1-2 lines). Per ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md feedback-authoring contract.
body_conventions.project_semantic: Lead with fact or decision + **Why:** (motivation, constraint, deadline) + **How to apply:** (how this shapes future suggestions). Project memories decay fast; the Why pins relevance.
body_conventions.user_semantic: Lead with the identity/preference statement; rationale optional but recommended for non-obvious preferences.
body_conventions.reference_semantic: Lead with the external-system pointer (URL or system name) + purpose (what consumer of the pointer needs to know).
body_conventions.episode_episodic_coala: Per CoALA paper (arXiv 2309.02427). Sections: ## Situation (1-2 lines: what triggered the session) → ## Thought (1-3 lines: model interpretation / decision frame) → ## Action (1-3 lines: what was done) → ## Result (1-3 lines: outcome + downstream signal). Authored by hooks/session-episode-write.sh.

legacy_field_aliases._description: Fields the corpus carries today under legacy names. The new field name is authoritative; legacy names will continue to be accepted (additionalProperties: true) and the staleness/staleness-derived capabilities will read the canonical name. Adopter migration is opt-in (no forced rewrite).
legacy_field_aliases.last_verified: → last_validated (canonical for the single 180d re-validation signal).

_design_notes.anthropic_load_contract: The harness loads only the first 200 lines OR 25KB of MEMORY.md (whichever comes first; documented at code.claude.com/docs/en/memory). This per-file schema governs frontmatter for files referenced FROM MEMORY.md; the MEMORY.md cap itself is enforced by R-59 (governance/mandatory-files-rules.json + hooks/pre-write-guard.sh advisory).
consumers: hooks/session-episode-write.sh (episodic capture; required to emit conformant frontmatter)
_design_notes.schema_version_policy: SemVer. Additive field additions = minor bump. Required-field changes or enum reductions = major bump (R-37 atomic lockstep with consumers above). The 1.0.0 → 2.0.0 bump dropped the `reflective` enum value (4 → 3, enum reduction = MAJOR) and promoted last_validated to required.

name.description: Short slug identifying this memory. SHOULD match the filename stem (kebab-case) when feasible. Used by the [[wikilink]] graph (related[] entries point to this slug).

description.description: RETRIEVAL HOOK — not a topic summary. Lead with the rule, trigger, or fact so a future-session relevance check happens in <100 tokens. Anti-pattern: 'Notes on tagging' (burns scan budget). Good: 'Every non-exempt vault file carries tags; orphans in graph view = hygiene alert.'

type.description: Retrieval-axis classification. See _design_notes.two_axes.retrieval_axis_type_field for value semantics. Orthogonal to the filename-prefix provenance axis. `reflective` was dropped at the 2.0.0 MAJOR bump — reflection is a consolidation process that rides the feedback_ provenance prefix, not a storage type.

tags.description: Free-form retrieval tags. May be empty []; presence-of-key required as a hygiene baseline (signals the author considered tag coverage at write time).

created.description: Memory authoring date (YYYY-MM-DD). Auto-stamped on file create by hooks/pre-write-guard.sh. Immutable after first write.

updated.description: Last edit date (YYYY-MM-DD). Auto-stamped on every write by hooks/pre-write-guard.sh. Does NOT reset the re-validation clock (last_validated is the sole decay input).

last_validated.description: Last date an operator confirmed this memory is still true (YYYY-MM-DD). REQUIRED (promoted at the 2.0.0 MAJOR bump). Bootstrap value = created when first introduced; auto-stamped on adopter writes by hooks/memory-auto-stamp.sh (fresh installs are conformant — no migration). The SOLE decay input for the single 180-day re-validation signal.

confidence.description: Confidence in memory accuracy. low = experimental hypothesis; medium = inferred from observation; high = explicitly confirmed by operator. Consumed for supersession tie-break (a high memory can't be auto-superseded by a lower one) and within-section index sort. Absent = no-op (NOT imputed medium).

supersedes.description: Slug of the memory file this one replaces (without .md extension). Drives audit-time deduplication and supersedes-chain traversal.

superseded_by.description: Slug of the memory file that replaces this one (without .md extension). Set when retiring a memory in place; readers MUST follow the pointer to the new authority before applying.

scope.description: Visibility / applicability scope. 'global' = applies everywhere (default if absent; the globalize-to-RULES candidate marker). 'project:<slug>' = scoped to a single plan slug. 'engagement:<name>' = scoped to a single engagement folder. Future retrieval-side filtering will key on this field.

related.description: Slugs of related memories (without .md extension). Drives the [[wikilink]] graph used by retrieval-time scoring. Liberal linkage encouraged; a related slug that doesn't yet exist as a file is fine — it marks a memory worth writing later.

source_session_id.description: Originating Claude session UUID. REQUIRED on type=episodic (the session lineage is the load-bearing field for replay). Optional on other types; useful as a provenance pointer when a non-trivial memory crystallized from a specific session.

then.description: Episodic memories require source_session_id so a future session can pull the originating-session record. Enforced for episodic capture-hook output.

examples.name: no-calendar-gates
examples.description: Calendar gates (e.g., 'wait 30 days') in plan close-out are arbitrary; prefer volume / data / event-driven gates. Audit is permanent infrastructure, not a campaign.

examples.name: vault-operating-philosophy
examples.description: Capture is cheap, the assistant organizes, systems thinking, historical data is sacred.

examples.name: episode-2026-05-24-mvp-spec
examples.description: MVP spec authored after the path-selection fork.
